agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (revised
April 21, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the
vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bsaleaumua@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

MINUTES
  MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JULY 26, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED - VARIO US LOCATIONS
  9:00A.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Cherin called the meeting to order at 9:08 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Lotte Cherin, Vice Chair Julia Holland; Commissioners Barry
  Haldeman, Peter Jones, and Fireball Lawrence; and Ex-Officio Clifford

  ALSO PRESENT: Jesse Bobbett, Community Services Director; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Deputy Director; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Ex-Officio Clifford led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CITY OF MALIBU VISION STATEMENT

  Commissioner Jones read the City of Malibu Vision Statement.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland moved, and Chair Cherin seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was properly
  posted on July 21, 2022.

ITEM I  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Election of Chair and Vice Chair

  Chair Cherin opened the floor for Chair nominations.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of July 26, 2022
  Page 2 of7

  Commissioner Haldeman stated Chair Cherin and Vice Chair Holland should
  remain as the Chair and Vice Chair.

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland nominated Commissioner Lawrence for Chair.

  Commissioner Jones indicated agreement with Commissioner Haldeman.

MOTION  Chair Cherin nominated herself for Chair.

  Chair Cherin closed the nominations for Chair.

  The question was called, and Chair Cherin, Commissioners Haldeman, Jones, and
  Lawrence voted for Chair Cherin, and Vice Chair Holland voted for Commissioner
  Lawrence. Chair Cherin was elected to serve as Chair.

  Chair Cherin opened the floor for Vice Chair nominations.

MOTION  Commissioner Jones nominated Vice Chair Holland for Vice Chair.

MOTION  Commissioner Lawrence nominated himself for Vice Chair.

  Vice Chair Holland declined the nomination.

  Chair Cherin closed the floor for Vice Chair nominations.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously. Commissioner
  Lawrence was elected to serve as Vice Chair.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  1.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo stated Commissions should
  have received a mailed copy of the 2022 Poetry and Art student anthology.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Deputy
  Director Riesgo stated the City could not sell the anthology, but would
  accept a donation, which would be added to the art donation account.

  In response to Vice Chair Lawrence, Community Services Deputy Director
  Riesgo stated the 2021-2022 Fiscal Year Arts Budget included funds to
  print the anthology.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of July 26, 2022
  Page 3 of7

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Chair Cherin stated she visited the "Art of Surf" exhibition at the Malibu
  City Gallery and commended Vice Chair Lawrence and Commissioner
  Holland for their work on the exhibition.

  Commissioner Haldeman and Ex-Officio Clifford indicated agreement with
  Chair Cherin.

  Commissioner Holland stated many people attended the Opening
  Reception. She stated the Ad Hoc focused on the surf theme and quality of
  work when they choose the featured artists.

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked the Commission for their comments and
  stated it was a team effort between Commissioner Holland, staff, and
  himself. He stated the featured artwork was choosen because there was an
  emotional connection to the work.

  Commissioner Haldeman suggested including directional signs for the
  Malibu City Gallery outside of Malibu City Hall.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Community Services Director Bobbett stated
  A-frames could be place outside of Malibu City Hall. He stated staff would
  research banners and signage for Pacific Coast Highway and Webb Way.

  Commissioner Lawrence stated he would contact staff to discuss Malibu
  City Hall signage.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  No updates.

  4.  Social Media

  No updates.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  This item was continued to the August 23, 2022 Regular meeting.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of July 26, 2022
  Page 4 of7

  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the May 24, 2022 Malibu
  Arts Commission Regular Meeting.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification
  Project; and 2) Provide direction to staff.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff report.

  Caltrans representative, Hammer Sui, presented an overview of the Project.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Mr. Sui stated the art budget was $225,000.

  Mr. Sui stated CalTrans would enter a cooperative agreement with the City of
  Malibu which would include details related to the artist and artwork selection by
  the Commission. He stated the artwork would need to be completed by June 2023
  and displayed at an off-site location for three years. He also stated Ca]Trans wanted
  the City to maintain the artwork once it is permanently installed.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Caltrans representative Vathana Chy stated the
  artwork would be 6 feet high to deter vandalism.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Mr. Sui stated the City would select the off-site
  location to display the artwork during the tunnel reconstruction period.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Community Services Director Bobbett stated
  the culvert reconstruction was related to the conservation of steelhead trout.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated there would be pedestrian access along Solstice Canyon.

  Chair Cherin suggested a Call for Artists selection process with an outside jury to
  review submissions and select the artist.

  Commissioner Lawrence indicated opposition to utilizing an outside jury to select
  the artwork.

  Topanga Art Tile owner, Matt Doolin, stated a tile art installation would require
  minimal maintenance.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Mr. Sui stated he would confirm with a
  CalTrans geologist to determine if an earthquake would affect the artwork.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of July 26, 2022
  Page 5 of7

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Mr. Sui stated Caltrans would consider
  extending the artwork to the ceiling. He stated the budget was the primary limitation
  for the project.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Mr. Sui stated artwork lighting would require a review
  and approval by CalTrans.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Mr. Doolin stated he could create organic shapes
  with tile similar to the artwork on Fire Station 71.

  Commissioner Holland stated the Commission should focus on selecting an artist
  and artwork medium. She suggested the Commission select Mr. Doolin as the artist.

  Chair Cherin stated the Commission should consider all mediums, and a Call for
  Artists would allow multiple artists an opportunity to submit a proposal.

  Commissioner Lawrence indicated opposition and believed the Commission should
  select Mr. Doolin as the project artist.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Chair Cherin.

  Mr. Chy stated the deadline for the completion of the cooperative artist agreement
  was October 31, 2022, and the artwork must be finished by June 2023.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Community Services Director Bobbett stated the
  agreement would be reviewed by the City Attorney, and would outline storage and
  maintenance responsibilities.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Mr. Sui stated $30,000 was budgeted for the
  storage of the artwork and administrative costs in addition to the $225,000 project
  budget for the Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Mr. Sui stated the Malibu Arts
  Commission would determine the artwork design and CalTrans would need
  information regarding the installation process.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Mr. Sui stated CalTrans would provide funding for the
  final artwork installation in the culvert, separate from the $255,000 budget.

  At 11 :00 a.m., Vice Chair Lawrence left the meeting.

MOTION  Chair Cherin moved, and Commissioner Haldeman seconded a motion to create a
  Call for Artists for the Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project. The question
  was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Vice Chair Lawrence absent.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of July 26, 2022
  Page 6 of7

  B.  Malibu Arts Budget
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report regarding the Adopted Malibu
  Arts Budget for Fiscal Year 2022-2023.

  This item was continued to the August 23, 2022 Regular meeting.

  C.  Malibu Arts Center
  Recommended Action: Discuss ideas for an arts center in Malibu.

  This item was continued to the August 23, 2022 Regular meeting.

  A.  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad

  This item was continued to the August 23, 2022 Regular meeting.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  This item was continued to the August 23, 2022 Regular meeting.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  This item was continued to the August 23, 2022 Regular meeting.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Arts Budget
  Arts Center
  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 11:07 a.m., Chair Cherin, and Commissioner Holland seconded a motion to
  adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Vice
  Chair Lawrence absent.
